description: Granular GB/day sizing rates. All values are in GB/day per unit. Override at vendor/model level where available.
disclaimer: These GB/day estimates are planning benchmarks only, not guarantees. Volume varies by retention, logging verbosity, sampling, vendor defaults, and traffic. Validate in your environment before procurement or contract commitments.

firewall_logs.unitDescription: Number of firewall appliances/instances generating logs
firewall_logs.helpText: Use the number of firewall devices sending logs. For virtual firewalls, count each vFW as one device. For cloud firewalls, count each policy set.
firewall_logs.notes: Highly variable based on traffic volume, logging scope, and user count behind device. Networks with 1000+ concurrent users per device trend toward high end.

Palo Alto Networks.notes: PA-Series tends to generate more verbose traffic logs. Threat logs add 10-20%.

Fortinet.notes: FortiGate traffic logs tend to be slightly more compact than Palo Alto.

Cisco ASA/FTD.notes: ASA syslog volume depends heavily on ACL logging verbosity.

Check Point.notes: Check Point Log Exporter format. SmartEvent adds additional volume.

edr_logs.unitDescription: Number of managed endpoints (laptops, desktops, servers) with EDR agent
edr_logs.helpText: Count all devices with the EDR agent installed. Include both workstations and servers if both are covered.
edr_logs.notes: Volume varies significantly by vendor and telemetry level. Server endpoints typically generate 2-3x more than workstations.

CrowdStrike Falcon.notes: FDR (Falcon Data Replicator) streaming to Splunk. Volume depends on FDR filter configuration.

Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.notes: Streaming via M365 Defender API or direct Splunk integration. Generally lower volume than CrowdStrike FDR.

SentinelOne.notes: Deep Visibility data via syslog or API. Volume scales with telemetry depth setting.

Carbon Black.notes: CB Response generates higher volume than CB Defense due to process tree depth.

windows_security_event_log.unitDescription: Number of Windows servers sending security event logs
windows_security_event_log.helpText: Count Windows servers with audit policies configured. Domain controllers typically generate 3-5x more than member servers.
windows_security_event_log.notes: Highly dependent on audit policy. Domain controllers with advanced audit policies can generate 0.5+ GB/day each.
windows_security_event_log.source: Windows audit policy documentation and field measurements

sysmon_logs.unitDescription: Number of endpoints/servers with Sysmon installed
sysmon_logs.helpText: Sysmon volume depends heavily on the XML configuration. Olaf Hartong's modular config is a common baseline.
sysmon_logs.notes: Extremely configuration-dependent. Untuned Sysmon on busy servers can generate 0.5+ GB/day. A well-tuned config (e.g., Olaf Hartong modular) typically generates 0.02-0.05 GB/day per endpoint. Rates validated against SwiftOnSecurity and modular config benchmarks.
sysmon_logs.source: Community benchmarks, Sysmon modular config documentation, and field deployment experience

active_directory_security.unitDescription: Number of Active Directory domain controllers
active_directory_security.helpText: Count domain controllers in each AD domain. Busy DCs with LDAP-heavy applications generate significantly more.
active_directory_security.notes: Includes Security, Directory Service, and DNS logs from DCs. LDAP-heavy environments trend toward high end.

okta_sso.helpText: Use total active Okta user count. API-heavy tenants or those with extensive MFA generate more.
okta_sso.notes: Includes system log events. Volume scales linearly with user count and login frequency.

m365_audit_logs.helpText: Total M365 E3/E5 users. E5 licenses generate more telemetry due to advanced audit features.
m365_audit_logs.notes: Includes Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams audit logs. DLP events can add significant volume.

aws_cloudtrail.unitDescription: Number of AWS accounts sending CloudTrail logs
aws_cloudtrail.helpText: Count AWS accounts with CloudTrail enabled. Data events (S3/Lambda) dramatically increase volume.
aws_cloudtrail.notes: Management events are relatively small (~0.1-0.5 GB/day per account). Enabling S3 data events or Lambda invocation logging can 10x+ the volume per account. Low confidence retained due to extreme variability with data events enabled.
aws_cloudtrail.source: AWS CloudTrail documentation and field deployments

vpn_logs.helpText: Count concurrent or total VPN users. Always-on VPN generates more than on-demand.
vpn_logs.notes: Primarily connection/disconnection events. Full tunnel logging increases volume.

proxy_web_gateway.unitDescription: Number of proxy/SWG appliances or virtual instances
proxy_web_gateway.helpText: Count proxy appliances or gateway instances. For cloud SWG, count logical proxy nodes or PoPs forwarding logs.
proxy_web_gateway.notes: Volume depends on browsing patterns and logging verbosity. Full URL logging generates significantly more than category-only.

dns_logs.unitDescription: Number of DNS servers/resolvers generating logs
dns_logs.helpText: Count internal DNS servers or resolvers. AD-integrated DNS for small orgs trends toward the low end.
dns_logs.notes: DNS query logging can be extremely high volume. Consider passive DNS or sampled logging if full query capture exceeds budget. Per-user rate validated against Infoblox and Microsoft DNS query log deployments.
dns_logs.source: DNS infrastructure benchmarks, Infoblox and Microsoft DNS deployment data

linux_auth.unitDescription: Number of Linux/Unix servers sending auth logs
linux_auth.helpText: Count servers sending syslog auth data (/var/log/auth.log or /var/log/secure).
linux_auth.notes: Includes sshd, sudo, PAM events. Web-facing servers with frequent SSH scans generate more.

netflow_data.helpText: Count routers/switches/firewalls exporting flow data. Core routers generate significantly more than edge.
netflow_data.notes: Extremely variable. A single core router in a large network can generate 5+ GB/day. Sampling rate (1:100 vs 1:1) dramatically affects volume. Low confidence retained due to infrastructure-specific variability. Rates represent 1:100 sampled flow baseline.
netflow_data.source: Network flow monitoring benchmarks and Cisco NetFlow documentation

vulnerability_scanner.helpText: Count unique IPs/hosts scanned per cycle. Volume is batch-oriented, not continuous.
vulnerability_scanner.notes: Vuln scan data is typically batch imported. Daily volume depends on scan frequency and asset count.

application_logs.helpText: Count distinct applications. Microservices architectures may have dozens to hundreds of services.
application_logs.notes: Wildly variable. A single busy Java application can generate 1+ GB/day. Logging level (INFO vs DEBUG) is the primary driver. Rates assume INFO-level logging in production. Low confidence retained due to inherent application-specific variability.
application_logs.source: Application monitoring benchmarks and JVM/Node.js deployment data

kubernetes_logs.helpText: Count worker nodes in the cluster. Control plane nodes add additional volume.
kubernetes_logs.notes: Includes container stdout/stderr, kube-system logs, and events. High-churn clusters with frequent deployments generate more. Per-node rate validated against SC4K (Splunk Connect for Kubernetes) deployment benchmarks.
kubernetes_logs.source: Kubernetes monitoring benchmarks and SC4K deployment data

active_directory.helpText: Mapped to domain-controller-centric rates (`active_directory_security`). Busy LDAP apps inflate LDAP-related events.
active_directory.notes: Conceptually mapped from legacy key `active_directory_security` for continuity with existing benchmark table; refine per vendor deployment.

apm.helpText: Distributed traces and code-level spans can dwarf log lines; confirm if traces vs. logs are in scope.
apm.notes: Distributed traces and code-level spans can exceed log volume significantly. Rates assume trace sampling at 10-20% in production. Full-fidelity tracing can 5x+ the high estimate.

app_servers.helpText: JVM/.NET app logging levels dominate; treat DEBUG as out-of-band for budget baselines.
app_servers.notes: Catalog-aligned benchmark for Application Servers. Cross-check overlaps with related legacy keys where applicable (e.g., SaaS vs. dedicated appliance logging).
